sa: द्वे अक्षरे ब्रह्मपरे त्व् अनन्ते विद्याविद्ये निहिते यत्र गूढे  ।
क्षरं त्व् अविद्या ह्य् अमृतं तु विद्या विद्याविद्ये ईशते यस् तु सो ऽन्यः ॥
iast: dve akṣare brahmapare tv anante vidyāvidye nihite yatra gūḍhe  ।
kṣaraṃ tv avidyā hy amṛtaṃ tu vidyā vidyāvidye īśate yas tu so ’nyaḥ ॥

alt.text: Both of these in the Transcendent, the Knowledge & the Ignorance, yea both have their hidden being in the Eternal & Infinite Who dwelleth beyond Brahman of the Veda, & are set in it for ever. But of these Ignorance dieth and Knowledge liveth for ever; and He who is master of both is other than they.

tr.text: Ignorance leads to the perishable. Wisdom leads to immortality. Entirely different from these is he, the imperishable, infinite, secret, Supreme Brahman, in whom exists wisdom as well as ignorance, and who governs them both.

sa: यो योनिं योनिम् अधितिष्ठत्य् एको विश्वानि रूपाणि योनीश् च सर्वाः  ।
ऋषिं प्रसूतं कपिलं यस् तम् अग्रे ज्ञानैर् बिभर्ति जायमानं च पश्येत् ॥
iast: yo yoniṃ yonim adhitiṣṭhaty eko viśvāni rūpāṇi yonīś ca sarvāḥ  ।
ṛṣiṃ prasūtaṃ kapilaṃ yas tam agre jñānair bibharti jāyamānaṃ ca paśyet ॥

alt.text: He being One entereth upon womb & womb, yea upon all forms of being and upon all wombs of creatures. This was He that of old filled with many sorts of Knowledge Kapila, the seer, after his mother bore him; yea He saw Kapila shaping.

words: brown or tawny or reddish colour; a kind of mouse; a kind of ape

tr.text: He alone presides over Nature in all aspect, and controls every form and every cause of production. He witnesses the birth of the first born seer of golden colour and nourishes him with wisdom.

sa: एकैकं जालं बहुधा विकुर्वन्न् अस्मिन् क्षेत्रे संहरत्य् एष देवः  ।
भूयः सृष्ट्वा पतयस् तथेशः सर्वाधिपत्यं कुरुते महात्मा ॥
iast: ekaikaṃ jālaṃ bahudhā vikurvann asmin kṣetre saṃharaty eṣa devaḥ  ।
bhūyaḥ sṛṣṭvā patayas tatheśaḥ sarvādhipatyaṃ kurute mahātmā ॥

alt.text: God weaveth Him one net or He weaveth Him another and He maketh it of manifold meshes & casteth it abroad in this field of the body; then He draweth it in again. Also He created Yatis, great Seekers, & thus the Mighty Mind wieldeth the sceptre of His universal Lordship.

words: a net; a hairnet; a net (fig.)
to bring or draw together; to unite; to compress
to have someone fly; fallen; fliegen

tr.text: Differentiating each genus into its species, and each species into its members, the Supreme Being withdraws them once more into their own ground. Again, bringing forth the agents of creation, the Great Self holds sway over them all.

sa: सर्वा दिश ऊर्ध्वम् अधश् च तिर्यक् प्रकाशयन् भ्राजते यद् वानड्वान्  ।
एवं स देवो भगवान् वरेण्यो योनिस्वभावान् अधितिष्ठत्य् एकः ॥
iast: sarvā diśa ūrdhvam adhaś ca tiryak prakāśayan bhrājate yad vānaḍvān  ।
evaṃ sa devo bhagavān vareṇyo yonisvabhāvān adhitiṣṭhaty ekaḥ ॥

alt.text: The Sun riseth & driveth the world’s wain, then he blazeth illumining all the regions and above and below and the level grow one lustre, even so this glorious & shining God, being One, entereth upon & ruleth nature that clingeth to the womb, to each womb its nature.

words: to make visible; to cause to appear or shine; to illumine

tr.text: Just as the sun shines lighting up all space above, below and across, even so does that one adorable God, the repository of all goodness and greatness, preside over everything that has the nature of a cause.

sa: यच् च स्वभावं पचति विश्वयोनिः पाच्यांश् च सर्वान् परिणामयेद् यः  ।
सर्वम् एतद् विश्वम् अधितिष्ठत्य् एको गुणांश् च सर्वान् विनियोजयेद् यः ॥
iast: yac ca svabhāvaṃ pacati viśvayoniḥ pācyāṃś ca sarvān pariṇāmayed yaḥ  ।
sarvam etad viśvam adhitiṣṭhaty eko guṇāṃś ca sarvān viniyojayed yaḥ ॥

alt.text: For He who is the Womb of the World bringeth each nature to its perfection and He matureth all those that are yet to be perfected. He indwelleth & presideth over all this His world and setteth all the modes of Nature to their workings.

words: to cause to cook or be cooked; to have cooked or to cook; to cause to ripen
to make ripe; to ripen; to mature
to entrust anything (acc.) to; to offer or present; to anything (acc.) to (dat.)

tr.text: He who is the one source of the world brings out everything out of His own Nature, and leads creatures to perfection according to their deserts, and endows each being with its distinguishing characteristic. Thus he presides over the whole universe.

sa: तद् वेदगुह्योपनिषत्सु गूढं तद् ब्रह्मा वेदते ब्रह्मयोनिं  ।
ये पूर्वं देवा ऋषयश् च तद् विदुस् ते तन्मया अमृता वै बभूवुः ॥
iast: tad vedaguhyopaniṣatsu gūḍhaṃ tad brahmā vedate brahmayoniṃ  ।
ye pūrvaṃ devā ṛṣayaś ca tad vidus te tanmayā amṛtā vai babhūvuḥ ॥

alt.text: This is that secret mystery which is hidden in Upanishads; for the Upanishad is the secret of the Veda. This is that which Brahma knoweth for the Womb of the Eternal and the older Gods and the sages who knew of This, became This & were immortal.

tr.text: He lies hidden in the Upanishads, which form the essence of the Vedas. Him the Hiranyagarbha knows as the source of Himself and the Vedas. Those gods and seers who realized Him in former days became identified with Him, and verily became immortal.

sa: गुणान्वयो यः फलकर्मकर्ता कृतस्य तस्यैव स चोपभोक्ता  ।
स विश्वरूपस् त्रिगुणस् त्रिवर्त्मा प्राणाधिपः संचरति स्वकर्मभिः ॥
iast: guṇānvayo yaḥ phalakarmakartā kṛtasya tasyaiva sa copabhoktā  ।
sa viśvarūpas triguṇas trivartmā prāṇādhipaḥ saṃcarati svakarmabhiḥ ॥

alt.text: There is One who maketh works and their fruits to them, for the moods of Nature cleave to Him; this is He that enjoyeth the works He hath done; and the World is His body and He hath three modes of His natures & the roads of His travel are likewise three. Lo, the Master of Life, by the momentum of His own works He moveth in the centuries.

words: one who enjoys or makes use of; an enjoyer; possessor
containing the three guṇas; consisting of 3 threads; threefold
to go or come together; to meet; to join

tr.text: Only he who gets attached to the pleasurable qualities of things does work for the sake of its fruits, and enjoys the fruits of his own deeds. Though really the master of the senses, he becomes bound by the three Gunas, and assuming various forms, wanders about through the three paths as a result of his own deeds.

sa: अङ्गुष्ठमात्रो रवितुल्यरूपः संकल्पाहंकारसमन्वितो यः  ।
बुद्धेर् गुणेनात्मगुणेन चैव आराग्रमात्रो ह्य् अवरो ऽपि दृष्टः ॥
iast: aṅguṣṭhamātro ravitulyarūpaḥ saṃkalpāhaṃkārasamanvito yaḥ  ।
buddher guṇenātmaguṇena caiva ārāgramātro hy avaro ’pi dṛṣṭaḥ ॥

alt.text: His size is as the size of a man’s thumb but His aspect as the Sun in its glory; and He hath Volition and He hath Personality; but there is another whom we see by virtue of the Understanding & by virtue of the Spirit for the point of a cobbler’s awl is not finer to vision.

words: a particular form of the sun (sometimes regarded as one of the 12 Ādityas); Sunday
conception of one's individuality; self-consciousness; the making of self
connected or associated with; completely possessed of; fully endowed with

tr.text: Subtle as the point of a goad, and pure, effulgent and infinite like the sun, He alone is seen assuming as another the size of a thumb on account of the finiteness of the heart (in which He appears), and associating Himself with egoism and Sankalpa on account of the limitations of the intellect.

sa: वालाग्रशतभागस्य शतधा कल्पितस्य च  ।
भागो जीवः स विज्ञेयः स चानन्त्याय कल्पते ॥
iast: vālāgraśatabhāgasya śatadhā kalpitasya ca  ।
bhāgo jīvaḥ sa vijñeyaḥ sa cānantyāya kalpate ॥

alt.text: Take thou the hundredth part of the point of a hair, divide it into a hundred parts again; then as is a part of this hundredth part of a hundredth, such shalt thou find this Spirit in man, if thou seek to separate Him; yet ’tis this in thee that availeth towards Infinity.

words: the hair of any animal's tail (esp. of a horse's tail); any tail or hair; bristle
in a hundred ways; a hundred-fold; into a hundred parts or pieces

tr.text: That individual soul is as subtle as a hairpoint divided and sub-divided hundreds of times. Yet he is potentially infinite. He has to be known.

sa: नैव स्त्री न पुमान् एष न चैवायं नपुंसकः  ।
यद् यच् छरीरम् आदत्ते तेन तेन स युज्यते ॥
iast: naiva strī na pumān eṣa na caivāyaṃ napuṃsakaḥ  ।
yad yac charīram ādatte tena tena sa yujyate ॥

alt.text: Not woman is He, nor man either, nor yet sexless; but whatsoever body He take, that confineth & preserveth Him.

words: to yoke or join or fasten or harness (horses or a chariot)

tr.text: He is neither female, nor male, nor neuter. Whatever body he assumes, he becomes identified with that.

sa: संकल्पनस्पर्शनदृष्टिमोहैर् ग्रासाम्बुवृष्ट्या चात्मविवृद्धिजन्म  ।
कर्मानुगान्य् अनुक्रमेन देही स्थानेषु रूपाण्य् अभिसंप्रपद्यते ॥
iast: saṃkalpanasparśanadṛṣṭimohair grāsāmbuvṛṣṭyā cātmavivṛddhijanma  ।
karmānugāny anukramena dehī sthāneṣu rūpāṇy abhisaṃprapadyate ॥

alt.text: As body is born and groweth by food and drink and plenty, so also the Spirit in body progressively attaineth to successive forms in their fit places — by the allurements of sight, by the witcheries of touch, by the magic of volition, for according to his works he progresseth and his forms shape themselves to his works.

words: the act of touching; touch; contact
a mouthful; lump (of rice etc. of the size of a peacock's egg); food
water; a kind of Andropogon; name of a metre (consisting of ninety syllables)
to be changed to; to assume or obtain the shape of (acc.)

tr.text: By desire, contact, sight and delusion, the embodied soul assumes successively various forms in various places according to his deeds, just as the body grows nourished by showers of food and drink.

sa: स्थूलानि सूक्ष्माणि बहूनि चैव रूपाणि देही स्वगुणैर् वृणोति  ।
क्रियागुणैर् आत्मगुणैश् च तेषां संयोगहेतुर् अपरो ऽपि दृष्टः ॥
iast: sthūlāni sūkṣmāṇi bahūni caiva rūpāṇi dehī svaguṇair vṛṇoti  ।
kriyāguṇair ātmaguṇaiś ca teṣāṃ saṃyogahetur aparo ’pi dṛṣṭaḥ ॥

alt.text: Forms gross and forms subtle, forms many, — the Spirit in body evolveth them all by his own nature in its working; by the law of action of his works & the law of action of the Spirit in man, by these he evolveth them. But there is Another in Whom we behold Cause whereby all these meet together.

tr.text: The embodied self chooses many forms, gross and subtle, based on the qualities belonging to himself, to the actions, and to the mind. The cause of their combination is found to be still another.

sa: अनाद्यनन्तं कलिलस्य मध्ये विश्वस्य स्रष्टारम् अनेकरूपं  ।
विश्वस्यैकं परिवेष्टितारं ज्ञात्वा देवं मुच्यते सर्वपाशैः ॥
iast: anādyanantaṃ kalilasya madhye viśvasya sraṣṭāram anekarūpaṃ  ।
viśvasyaikaṃ pariveṣṭitāraṃ jñātvā devaṃ mucyate sarvapāśaiḥ ॥

alt.text: Without beginning, without end in the welter and the chaos, who createth the world by taking many figures & as the One girdeth & encompasseth it. He is the Lord & if thou know Him thou shalt break free from all kinds of bondage.

words: one who emits or discharges (water etc.); a maker; author

tr.text: Realizing Him who is without beginning or end, who creates the cosmos in the midst of chaos, who assumes many forms, and who alone envelops everything, one becomes free from all fetters.

sa: भावग्राह्यम् अनीडाख्यं भावाभावकरं शिवं  ।
कलासर्गकरं देवं ये विदुस् ते जहुस् तनुम् ॥
iast: bhāvagrāhyam anīḍākhyaṃ bhāvābhāvakaraṃ śivaṃ  ।
kalāsargakaraṃ devaṃ ye vidus te jahus tanum ॥

alt.text: Shiva the Master of all becomings and not-becomings and from Him this whole creation floweth and it is only one part of Shiva; but He is not named after any nest of the wingèd Spirit, and the heart alone can apprehend Him. They who know Shiva, the Blessed One, abandon body for ever.

words: any place for settling down; resting-place; abode

tr.text: That Supreme Divinity who created both Life and Matter, who is the source of all arts and sciences, who can be intuited by a pure and devoted mind – realizing Him, the blissful the incorporeal and the nameless, one is freed from further embodiment.
